dialect.detail: JMA ORCA medical receipt software (JMA standard receipt software), likely compiled with GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL on Linux. Uses MCP (Message Control Program) interface pattern typical of ORCA system.

purpose.domain_detail: JMA ORCA standard medical receipt (claims) software - accounting card frequency-of-visit input screen (J022 window, visit count entry)
purpose.summary: This program handles the input screen for visit count (frequency) entry in the JMA ORCA medical receipt system. It processes user input for up to three visit-day fields (DAY1, DAY2, DAY3), validates numeric input via ORCSNUM subroutine, stores results in SPA working storage, and manages screen cursor positioning and window transitions. It is a subprogram called via the ORCA MCP linkage mechanism.

notable_features: Heavy use of COPY statements (27 copybooks) for ORCA framework includes
MCP event-driven screen handling (MCP-STATUS, MCP-EVENT, MCP-WIDGET)
LINKAGE SECTION with multiple screen area copybooks (J02.INC through JERR.INC)
CALL to ORCSNUM for numeric validation
CALL to ORCSDAY for date conversion
EVALUATE on MCP-STATUS/MCP-EVENT for event dispatch
Japanese EUC/Shift-JIS encoded comments (latin-1 decoded as mojibake)
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS
PERFORM VARYING loop over 31-day calendar array
verdict.notes: Comment text is Japanese encoded in EUC-JP or Shift-JIS, decoded as latin-1 resulting in mojibake. Program is part of the open-source JMA ORCA medical receipt system circa 2000-2002. The ORCA system runs on Linux with GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL. Fixed format with max line length 74 consistent with standard COBOL fixed format.
